derivations.quote: As $\mathsf SI\mathsf S=\operatorname{diag}(1,-1)$, $\mathsf SX\mathsf S=iX$, $ab=ib^2=\frac12$, direct multiplication gives $H_0=b\,\mathsf SC\mathsf S$, $C^2=X$, $C^4=I$

Gaussian elimination writes $M$ as at most $m(m-1)+3m$ row additions (a swap is three). So apply $\mathcal P_M^{-1}$ to each column, then $(C^{\epsilon_h})^{\otimes f}$ to the $f$ bits of slot $h$, then $\mathcal P_M$: one child on $f$ axes per residual vector. A negative kernel needs no inverse child, since $(C^{-1})^{\otimes f}=(-i)^fZ^{\otimes f}C^{\otimes f}Z^{\otimes f}$, $Z=\operatorname{diag}(1,-1)$. Summing residual dimensions gives exactly $s$ children, each on $f=e/m$ axes.

With $x_1,\dots,x_D$ the selected bits of an address $x$, this yields $H_0^{\otimes D}=b^D\mathcal S_DC^{\otimes D}\mathcal S_D$, $(\mathcal S_Dz)(x)=i^{x_1+\dots+x_D}z(x)$. The phases and $b^D=(-i/2)^{\lfloor D/2\rfloor}b^{D\bmod2}$ are exact Gaussian dyadic operations.
Each row addition XORs selected bits of two slots, done by [Packed selected-bit addition](packed-bit-addition.md). So the basis change and its inverse cost $O(V((eK)^\tau+1))$

Let $W$ be the network's wire count and $F(e)$ the time divided by volume. Apply $C$ individually to the first $q_0=\lceil\log_2W\rceil\lceil\log_m(2d)\rceil$ chunks and use their bits as a row index, padded to a multiple of $W^{k_0}$, $k_0=\lceil\log_md\rceil$. Row $Wg+w$ goes to wire $w$, so each child has volume $V/W$. The recurrence is solved as in [Recursive power saving](rank-recurrence.md): for $e\ge d^\beta$, $\beta=\frac12$, $F(e)\le(s/W)F(e/m)+O((eK)^\tau+1)$, and $F(e)=O(e)$ below. As $K\le d^c\le e^{c/\beta}$, the overhead is $O(e^\lambda)$ for fixed $\max\{\tau,\sigma\}<\lambda<1$. With $a=s/W\le m^\sigma<m^\lambda$, internal levels sum to $Ce^\lambda\sum_{j\ge0}(a/m^\lambda)^j=O(e^\lambda)$; leaves add $O(a^ju)\le O(e^\sigma u^{1-\sigma})\le O(e^\sigma d^{\beta(1-\sigma)})$. Base-$m$ pieces of the remaining chunks give $O(\log(2d)[d^\lambda+d^{\sigma+\beta(1-\sigma)}+1])=O(d^{\lambda'})$

Let $A(e)$ bound arithmetic operations along a chain: $A(e)\le sA(e/m)+E$, $E=64(W+m+1)^3$, and $A(e)\le8e$ at leaves. As $sx+E\le Bx$ for $B=s+E$, $A(e)\le8B^2d^{\nu+1}$ with $\nu=\min\{j\ge1:m^j\ge B\}$. After $\ell$ operations a value lies in $2^{-(p+\ell)}\mathbb Z[i]$ with modulus at most $2^\ell$: addition doubles modulus, halving adds a denominator bit. So with $\Delta=\lceil C_0d^{C_1}\rceil$, reserving $p+\Delta$ fractional bits and $\Delta+3$ integer and sign bits per real component, as in [Fixed-point Gaussian dyadic records](fixed-point.md), represents every intermediate coefficient exactly. If $d=\Theta(p^\epsilon)$ and $\epsilon C_1<1$, then $\Delta=o(p)$ and the width is $O(p)$.

Each row of $H_0$ has entries $\pm\frac12$, and row sums multiply under tensor products, so every row of $\mathcal H$ has absolute row sum one, hence $\mathcal H$ maps disk arrays (coefficients of modulus at most $1$) to disk arrays
$Q_p$ truncates each real component toward zero, which keeps the disk and changes each component by less than $2^{-p}$, so $\|Q_p(\mathcal Hz)-\mathcal Hz\|_\infty<\sqrt2\,2^{-p}$
